views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep negotiating in the Washington round without new tariff hikes, rollbacks, or purchase-only commitments. Push for written enforcement language and IP/tech-transfer text while leaving the unused List 3 hike to 25% on the table as leverage. Do not trade the Huawei/Meng cases for a deal and do not spend tariff leverage before a text is signed.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Net threat to US interests is roughly balanced as of 2019-04-03. Leverage is real: List 3 is still at 10% after the Feb 24 delay, the March 1 hike window passed unused, and about $250B of Chinese goods remain under Section 301, while April 3 talks reported progress on draft text including enforcement. US macro is not in crisis—Michigan sentiment 97.2, VIX 13.74, CNY firmer near 6.71. Offsetting that, costs are sectoral and political: IMPCH is down about 26% in the window, industrial production is off about 1.7%, and farm retaliation remains acute (record 3.7 billion bushels of soy in storage; China had taken about 60% of US soy exports). Escalating now would risk collapsing the closest approach to a text since Buenos Aires; conceding rollbacks before enforcement is signed would give away the remaining hike threat. Hold the current tariff stock and negotiate the unfinished structural issues.
key_factors: Washington talks reporting progress on enforcement text but no signed deal
Unused List 3 10-to-25% hike still held in reserve after Feb 24 delay
US sentiment and vol not signaling a trade-war emergency
Sharp drop in US imports from China and a modest IP dip
Soybean overhang and incomplete purchase pledges keep farm-belt pressure on
Huawei/Meng legal track should stay separate from tariff bargaining

sources_cited.excerpt: Intensive Washington talks; both sides report progress on text, including enforcement language. No final deal signed.
Talks made substantial progress; List 3 hike from 10% to 25% further delayed.
List 3 takes effect at 10%. Combined US Section 301 coverage now about $250B of Chinese imports.
G20 90-day window; planned Jan 1 List 3 hike suspended. Same day Canada arrests Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou on a US request.
US goods imports from China latest about $34.5B vs $46.3B in Nov 2018, about -26% over the window.
US industrial production slipped from 104.07 (Nov 2018) to 102.27 (Apr 2019), about -1.7%.
Michigan consumer sentiment recovered to 97.2 in April 2019 after a January dip to 91.2.
VIX at 13.74 on 2019-04-03, well below the Dec 2018 spike above 30.
CNY/USD strengthened from about 6.92 in Oct 2018 to 6.71 on 2019-04-03.
Kudlow: making good headway but not there yet; outstanding issues include IP protection and an enforcement mechanism.
US soybean stocks hit a record 3.7 billion bushels; pledged Chinese purchases would still leave a large overhang.
